answer: Temporal divergence validation requires every active node to continuously solve unique, hardware-bound cryptographic puzzles that cannot be parallelized or pre-computed. If a malicious operator spins up thousands of artificial clones to overwhelm the network, each duplicate receives identical execution inputs and returns an indistinguishable echo across the distributed ledger. The protocol flags this behavioral uniformity and systematically slashes the shared collateral anchor, draining the primary deposit of copper hardware tokens tied to the compromised subnet.
